author: Stoker Wieczorek
title: Former Republic cadet pilots Air Force flyover for high school's Salute to Veterans game - NewsBreak
text:
By Stoker Wieczorek ,
2 hours ago
REPUBLIC, Mo. — Republic High School is hosting a military flyover for its annual "Salute to Veterans" football game, featuring a U.S. Air Force trainer aircraft piloted by a former Republic High School cadet.
An Air Force T-6 Texan II turboprop trainer will fly in from Vance Air Force Base in Enid, Oklahoma, to perform the stadium flyby right as the National Anthem concludes before kickoff.
A hometown connection in the cockpit
At the controls of the T-6 Texan II is Air Force Captain Noah Johnson, who took aviation ground school in the hallways of Republic High School before graduating and attending the U.S. Air Force Academy.
For Republic High School Air Force JROTC Instructor Lt. Col. Patrick Sanders, watching his former cadet return home in uniform represents a full-circle moment.
"He came and talked to them about pilot training and what it takes," Lt. Col. Sanders said. "We've kept in good contact with each other, and it's just kind of fruits of my labor, I guess you could say, that I've got a cadet out there making a difference in the world and following his dreams."
Sanders noted that Johnson was always a focused student. "He was a self-driven cadet of mine... seeing him make a difference in the world and following his dreams, it's just kind of fruits of my labor."
Precise timing and a rare high school honor
Securing military authorization from Washington, D.C., for a high school flyover is extremely rare, as aerial passes are typically reserved for major college or professional sports venues.
"I've never heard of a flyby at a high school game ever before," Lt. Col. Sanders said. "Football games, college pros, of course, you see those on TV... so it's a pretty big honor for me to be able to do this."
To execute the flyby with split-second accuracy, the aircrew will orbit south of the stadium awaiting Sanders' cue.
"They're going to be taking off from Vance Air Force Base in Enid, Oklahoma, and they're going to be flying here and setting up an orbit to the south of the field," Sanders explained. "When I tell them the national anthem has started, they got a minute seven seconds to time it perfectly over the stadium."
Honoring local veterans on the 50-yard line
Following the pass over Republic's stadium, Captain Johnson will land the T-6 at Springfield-Branson National Airport before being escorted back to the high school to join local veterans on the 50-yard line during halftime.
The Salute to Veterans ceremony includes playing the official service songs for each military branch to recognize former and active-duty service members in attendance.
"Veterans in general tend to be shy," Sanders added. "They don't want to be recognized, which is fine. But given the chance, I think they can stand proud and be recognized by the population of people around them."
